data.narrative:
Varda Space Industries, a Series D space technology company founded by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov, has raised $329M to date against a current post-money valuation of $1.58B. The valuation analysis relies on a comp universe of 5 public Space & Aerospace equities (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers spanning similar and adjacent stages, including Apex Space, Sierra Space, and Skyryse.

Two valuation methods triangulate on Varda's fair value. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.5x step-up multiplier to the $1.5B last post-money, implying $2.2B. Peer-median anchoring across 3 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Sierra Space ($8.0B Series C), Apex Space ($2.3B Series D), and Skyryse ($1.1B Series C)—yields a median of $2.3B. Public-comp P/S anchoring is inapplicable due to absence of disclosed revenue. The public Space & Aerospace median multiple stands at 27.4x across the 6-ticker set.

The two applicable methods converge on a valuation range of $1.9B (low) to $2.6B (high), with a median of $2.3B. This range sits above Varda's current $1.58B valuation. Key uncertainties include wide dispersion in peer valuations ($1.1B–$8.0B), reflecting heterogeneous business models and commercial maturity within the space sector, and the absence of revenue visibility to anchor relative-value methods.
